prose:
The Financial Times describes a reversal in investor sentiment: software and semiconductor S&P 500 sub-indices were both slightly negative for the year at publication, with software ahead after chips bore more of the recent sell-off. The article contrasts software firms with data, customer and security advantages against businesses still exposed to disruption.

These are dated market observations and attributed interpretations, not a permanent ranking of AI winners or investment advice. Gains in selected cybersecurity names coexist with large declines in other software names, so the sector average does not establish that every firm benefits. Explanations involving AI, policy and data-center sentiment are reporting and analyst views rather than a causal decomposition independently tested here. No trade or current quote check was made.
highlights: Both reported sub-indices are marginally negative YTD
Security and infrastructure names differ from other software
Index returns do not measure product quality
No investment action or live quote verification occurred
